title: Mapping fibromyalgia: convergence of neurodevelopmental, neuroinflammatory, and pain matrix connectivity alterations
description:
Although fibromyalgia (FM) impacts up to 8% of the global population, the search for objective biomarkers continues to be hampered by the condition's vast patient heterogeneity. The precise pathophysiological mechanisms driving its development and chronicity remain elusive. Recent imaging studies suggest the role of central sensitization, the role of psychological distress is also documented, and multi-omics analysis points towards the involvement of inflammation.

Since integration across the different modalities is absent, we aimed to have a multi-method approach integrating baseline and acute pain-evoked fMRI, comprehensive psychological profiling and molecular signatures from peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) transcriptomics to explore the complexity of the psycho-neuro-immunological mechanisms.

Several inflammation- and neurodevelopment-related signaling pathways such as IL-12 signaling in macrophages, neutrophil degranulation, netrin signaling, synaptic long term potentiation, were altered in FM patients' PBMCs.

The results demonstrate altered central pain processing as well as interoceptive dominance with reduced epistemic openness as a central processing style in FM. Omics analysis suggests dysregulated immune-neural crosstalk, hyperactive innate immune-mediated inflammation, and impaired synaptic plasticity. Our findings depict a biologically sustained, psychologically modulated condition, necessitating the development of novel therapeutic guidelines to ensure effective treatment for identifying diagnostic/prognostic biomarkers to improve future treatment regimens.
